items.title: Fred Lipsius interviewed by Monk Rowe. Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: I still listen to Sonny Stitt, my heroes, Bird and all the old jazz players... listening to Charlie Parker, Coltrane... Those were my favorite.

ctx.x: Are we getting a lot of noise from that chair? Good. Okay. I’ll cut that part out. How have you seen the business change, of jazz education in the last ten or so years because of technology. The students that come to you, they’ve grown up in this everything is available on YouTube and on Spotify and so forth. Do you notice a difference in the students?

Well honestly the last ten years or so, I’ve been teaching mostly private saxophone. I’ve taught everything: jazz comp, arranging, all kinds of stuff. But some years ago I had found out more seriously that I had a hearing loss, probably from Blood, Sweat & Tears, from loud amp. So I got kind of panicky and said I don’t know if I can teach anymore. So I started teaching in the woodwind department, fifteen or twenty years ago. So I have my little room with a Yamaha upright piano and two people sit there and that’s…

new people. Personally I’m at a point in my life I don’t really want to be putting anybody down. We all have opinions, what we like, just like foods or, why did I pick my wife? You know? That simple. But as some spiritual master said a while back, and I try to live these principles now, you know instead of bringing out the bad in someone, if you have something bad to say, bring out the good, even if they’re bad people. Because it’s going to bring out the better in you and it’s going to maybe open their hearts a…
